evidence.source: Guarded Production rollout run 31505763706 applied contracts 159 to 171 as ONE boundary from exact main 0f778ffbde7825228379ea24624cc90a92c2fe0c, after its own API check that backup run 31500395326 and rehearsal run 31505339791 had both concluded success, and after a dry run that asserted the thirteen migration files BY NAME with diff rather than by count. Unlike contract 158, every migration in this range is ADDITIVE, so check-migration-additive.mjs ran as a GATE rather than as a report; a future reader who finds that softened back to a report should stop, because the boundary has changed. The rehearsal was not a formality: its FIRST dispatch, run 31504557398, failed at the Production dump with `supabase: command not found`, because both workflows were derived from the proven 157-to-158 pair and dropped its actions/setup-node and supabase/setup-cli steps. It failed on its own runner rather than part-way through a Production apply, which is the whole reason the gate exists. Everything upstream of the missing binary had already passed on that run, including the read-only confirmation that the live source was exactly contract 158 at 20260811000000. The steps were restored at the same pinned versions in run 31505339791, which then reached exactly contract 171 on a disposable target restored from a fresh Production dump. An independent read-only query through a different connection then confirmed the applied result rather than trusting the workflow's own: the ledger NAMES all thirteen rows 20260811100000_invite_resolver_probe_hardening through 20260811220000_league_prediction_cap_honesty sitting above 158's 20260811000000, and the total is 171. Naming the rows rather than counting them is deliberate and was learned the same day: a select count(*) against the DEVELOPMENT ledger returned a stale 168 for roughly twenty-five minutes after an apply had succeeded, while a row-level query on the same table in the same session returned the truth immediately, and that stale count nearly caused a successful rollout to be reported as a failure. The structural facts were verified in the same independent query. predictor_internal.cup_final_group_tables STILL carries `sequence between 1 and 3`: contract 169 added the season table beside the tournament's rather than widening it, and the tournament's production-hosted ranking authority — the one reached by admin_finalise_predictor_cup_groups, where under ADR 0014 a wrong group table decides qualification and seeding — is untouched. predictor_internal.cup_season_group_tables carries no matchday bound at all. Six new relations exist (season_table_rules, season_table_adjustments, season_fixture_awards, player_action_items, player_action_state, reminder_deliveries) and NONE is granted to anon or authenticated; process_player_action_items is reachable by neither browser role nor PUBLIC. Nothing player-owned moved across thirteen migrations: 1 auth user, 1 profile, 3 tournaments, 56 teams, 51 matches, 3 entries, 36 match predictions, 1 league, 1 league member, 0 score events, 3 entry totals, 7 game memberships, 10 competitions, 578 season fixtures and 10 season predictions, all unchanged. This is SCHEMA ONLY and claims nothing further. It did not publish Euro 2028 — contract 143's state stays hidden and publication is an owner act, and EURO-001 remains a recorded defect. It launched no competition, drew no Championship and opened no Last Man Standing, because contracts 166 and 127 write only when an administrator calls them. It scheduled no job: 0 cron jobs before and after, so contract 170 generates no action item until something calls the driver, and contract 163 sends nothing and names no provider. It imported no football, and copying Development football rows into Production remains forbidden by the contract 132 boundary. Application promotion is separately controlled and is NOT claimed by this record: the deployed site remains at contract 145, so no browser can reach any of this yet.
